title: podman inspect of a name that matches nothing acquires the lock of every container
body:
### Issue Description

`podman inspect NAME` with no `--type` walks the object types. When the name
matches nothing, it reaches the network stage, and `NetworkInspect`
unconditionally calls `GetContainerNetStatuses`, which iterates every container
and takes each container's lock to read its network status
(`pkg/domain/infra/abi/network.go:292` -> `libpod.(*Container).GetNetworkStatus`,
`libpod/container.go:1486`).

Two consequences:

* A lookup that resolves nothing takes N container locks.
* If any single container's lock is unavailable, `podman inspect` of a
  *nonexistent* name blocks forever — while `podman network ls`, which does not
  touch containers, returns immediately.

Using `podman inspect <tag>` as an image existence check is a common pattern,
and it runs precisely on the miss path, so a single stuck container is enough to
wedge it permanently. See https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29646 for how the container got stuck.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Have one container whose lock is held and not released (any long-held
   container lock will do).
2. `podman network ls` -> returns immediately.
3. `podman inspect some-name-that-does-not-exist` -> hangs forever.
4. `podman inspect --type image some-name-that-does-not-exist` -> returns
   immediately with rc=125.

### Describe the results you received

Measured with a 15 s timeout; rc=124 means it hung, rc=125 means "no such object":

    podman network ls                       rc=0
    podman image exists MISSING             rc=1
    podman inspect --type image MISSING     rc=125
    podman inspect --type container MISSING rc=125
    podman inspect --type pod MISSING       rc=125
    podman inspect --type volume MISSING    rc=125
    podman inspect --type network MISSING   rc=124   <-- hangs
    podman inspect MISSING (no --type)      rc=124   <-- hangs

Goroutine dump of the hanging process (`GOTRACEBACK=all`, then `SIGQUIT`):

    runtime.cgocall
    libpod/lock/shm._Cfunc_lock_semaphore(0x..., 0x4)
    libpod/lock/shm.(*SHMLocks).LockSemaphore(0x..., 0x4)
            libpod/lock/shm/shm_lock.go:227
    libpod/lock.(*SHMLock).Lock(...)
            libpod/lock/shm_lock_manager_linux.go:127
    libpod.(*Container).GetNetworkStatus(...)
            libpod/container.go:1486
    pkg/domain/infra/abi.(*ContainerEngine).GetContainerNetStatuses(...)
            pkg/domain/infra/abi/network.go:292
    pkg/domain/infra/abi.(*ContainerEngine).NetworkInspect(...)
            pkg/domain/infra/abi/network.go:72
    cmd/podman/inspect.(*inspector).inspect(...)
            cmd/podman/inspect/inspect.go:137
    cmd/podman/inspect.Inspect(...)
            cmd/podman/inspect/inspect.go:46

Note that semaphore 4 belongs to a container entirely unrelated to the name
being looked up, and that the requested network does not exist either.

### Describe the results you expected

Resolving a name that matches nothing should not require locking unrelated
containers. A network inspect that fails to find the network should not
enumerate container network statuses at all, and even on success it should not
need every container's lock just to answer "does this network exist".

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

Rootless podman built from upstream source, v5.8.0, commit
07efc23e05c3d9aa15a0f30d57194737bfc4b6b1, Go 1.24.2. Ubuntu 24.04,
kernel 6.8.0-124-generic, x86_64. Storage driver `overlay` on xfs with
`Native Overlay Diff: false`, runtime runc 1.3.3, DB backend sqlite, network
backend netavark 1.11.0, cgroup manager systemd.

### Additional information

Workaround: use `podman image exists NAME` (or `podman inspect --type image
NAME`), which stays on the image path and never touches container locks.
